title: ChartRequest Reviews 2026
summary: ChartRequest reviews, covering the company, its release-of-information product line, CaseBinder retrieval for law firms, turnaround, pricing, and security, plus how Codes Health adds AI litigation analysis on a flat fee.
body_markdown:
For plaintiff law firms, the retrieval vendor you pick shapes how fast a case moves and how much paralegal time disappears into provider follow-up. ChartRequest has been in the medical records business since 2012, though a lot of that history sits on the healthcare side rather than the legal one. This review covers the company, its product line, what CaseBinder actually does for law firms, and how it compares to a platform like[the Codes Health workflow](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) that pairs retrieval with litigation analysis.


## **Key Takeaways**


-


ChartRequest is a healthcare information technology and services company founded in 2012 in Atlanta, specializing in electronic medical record fulfillment, outsourced release of information, and referral management


-


CaseBinder is its legal product, offered in Self-Service and Full-Service configurations with a dedicated retrieval coordinator, guided request submission, e-authorization, and provider follow-up handled by its team


-


ChartRequest reports internal data showing an average 14 day turnaround for CaseBinder retrieval, noting actual times vary by request and provider


-


CaseBinder carries no monthly subscription fee, and ChartRequest advertises a 90-day introductory rate of $35 per request, with custom pricing after


-


ChartRequest's public materials do not advertise AI-powered litigation analysis such as automated chronologies, breach-in-care identification, or future expense extraction


-


Codes Health works toward complete records in a couple of weeks with retrieval, AI analysis, and human verification in one flat-fee workflow


-


Incomplete or invalid authorizations are a leading cause of rejected requests, and pre-submission AI validation catches them before a resubmission is needed


## **ChartRequest: Company Overview**


ChartRequest was founded in 2012 in Atlanta, Georgia, and describes itself as a healthcare information technology and services company specializing in electronic medical record fulfillment, outsourced medical record fulfillment, and referral management. Chris Carter serves as CEO.


The company's center of gravity is the release of information process, or ROI, the workflow providers follow when releasing a patient's records to an authorized party. ChartRequest sells software and services on both sides of that transaction: to the healthcare organizations fulfilling requests, and to the requestors submitting them, including law firms, insurance companies, and patients.


That dual audience matters when you're evaluating the company for legal work, because much of what ChartRequest publishes centers on the provider side of ROI rather than on litigation workflows.


### **The Product Line**


ChartRequest organizes its offering into several distinct products:


-


**ChartRequestPro:** a self-service platform letting healthcare teams manage record release in house through a guided workflow, centralized dashboard, and automated invoicing


-


**ChartRequestComplete:** a full-service option where the ChartRequest team handles release of medical, imaging, and billing records, advertised with a 5-day average turnaround time guarantee


-


**CaseBinder:** the retrieval product built for law firms and legal teams


-


**Referral management:** tools aimed at reducing referral leakage and improving coordination between providers


The company also supports subpoena-driven workflows, DICOM imaging, and certificates of authenticity, and describes its platform as EMR-agnostic, meaning it runs alongside whatever record system an organization already uses.


## **CaseBinder: What Law Firms Actually Get**


CaseBinder is the piece that matters for litigation teams, and ChartRequest has been selling into legal for more than a decade. It comes in two configurations.


**Self-Service** gives the firm control of the entire request process through the platform. Your team creates the account, submits requests, gathers authorizations, and tracks status. ChartRequest positions this for firms newer to retrieval software or without high request volumes.


**Full-Service** hands the work over. A dedicated retrieval coordinator manages the process end to end.


### **The Full-Service Workflow**


ChartRequest describes the process in five steps:


-


You submit through a guided request workflow that prompts for client, provider, authorization, and scope details before anything goes out


-


Retrieval experts handle all provider follow-up and escalate when a request stalls


-


The team verifies the production matches the request, including patient, date ranges, and record types


-


Anything falling outside the authorization gets redacted before release


-


Completed records are released to your dashboard for download


When records come back incomplete, ChartRequest says its team follows up with the provider rather than passing the gap along. That's a real verification step and worth being precise about, because CaseBinder is not a service that simply forwards whatever a provider sends.


### **Other CaseBinder Features**


-


E-authorization sent to a client's email or phone for e-signature


-


Real-time status tracking through a centralized dashboard


-


Certificates of authenticity available on request


-


Medical imaging retrieval where relevant to the case


-


Support for subpoena-driven workflows


-


Nationwide provider access, with ChartRequest advertising a large national network


### **Turnaround**


ChartRequest reports internal data showing an average of 14 days for medical record retrieval with CaseBinder, and states that actual times vary based on the request and the practice receiving it. The company also correctly notes that under HIPAA, providers generally have up to 30 days to respond to a records request with one possible extension, citing 45 CFR 164.524.


A separate figure of roughly 30 days appears in some company-wide materials, though that appears to describe ChartRequest operations broadly rather than the managed CaseBinder service.


## **Pricing**


CaseBinder carries no monthly partnership subscription fee. ChartRequest advertises a 90-day introductory rate of $35 per request with no upfront cost, after which pricing is customized.


The company also says retrieval fees scale down as request volume grows, and that Full-Service customers pay less per request than a basic account because the ChartRequest team absorbs the follow-up work. Provider and custodian copying fees are separate and vary by jurisdiction and record type.


What the introductory rate covers is the managed retrieval experience: dedicated retrieval experts, provider follow-up, real-time status, nationwide provider access, the dashboard, accuracy verification, and HIPAA-compliant security. It does not include AI chronologies or litigation analysis, since those aren't part of the advertised product.


## **Security and Compliance**


ChartRequest advertises 256-bit SSL, 2048-bit private keys, and multi-layered AES encryption for patient records, along with role-based access control determining who can view records based on their role in the ROI process. The platform requires every request to pass quality assurance verification twice.


The company also advertises SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001-aligned security on its legal pages. As with any vendor handling protected health information, confirm business associate agreement terms, data retention policies, and incident response procedures directly.


## **Customer Feedback and Market Presence**


ChartRequest publishes customer testimonials on its own site, including healthcare organizations describing it as a reliable records partner and legal staff crediting individual coordinators with walking them through requests.


Independent third-party review coverage is comparatively thin. ChartRequest maintains listings on software review directories, but published legal-sector review volume is limited next to larger litigation support vendors. Firms evaluating CaseBinder should ask for references from law firms with similar practice areas and caseloads rather than leaning on directory scores.


## **Where CaseBinder Stops and Analysis Begins**


Here's the honest line to draw. CaseBinder is a genuine managed retrieval operation with verification built in. What ChartRequest's public materials do not advertise is AI-powered analysis of the records once they arrive: automated medical chronologies, breach-in-care identification, future medical expense extraction, or proactive AI-driven gap detection across a patient's treatment history.


Firms using CaseBinder generally handle that through internal paralegal review or a separate analysis vendor. For some practices that's fine. For others it means the records land and the clock starts over on a different kind of work.


### **What Integrated Analysis Adds**


[The Codes Health platform](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) approaches the same problem by combining retrieval with analysis in one workflow:


-


**AI-powered case chronologies** grouping encounters and bills by visit, exposing treatment gaps, and preserving links back to source documents


-


**Breach-in-care identification** for medical malpractice work


-


**Documented future medical expenses** extracted for damages support


-


**Pre-existing condition flagging** and other hidden case facts


-


**Proactive missing record detection** cross-referencing patient history to find gaps before delivery


-


**Authorization validation** catching misspellings, missing signatures, unclear expiration dates, and missing dates of service before submission


All of it runs through human verification before delivery, which Codes Health describes as AI insights verified by humans. It works toward complete records in a couple of weeks on a flat fee.


Worth separating this from the general-purpose tools some firms try first. General AI platforms like ChatGPT are not designed for litigation-grade medical record review. They don't retrieve records, validate authorizations, follow up with providers, or verify completeness. Codes Health's platform is built for this work and analyzes records with high precision for legal teams.


On speed claims across the market, Codes Health notes that services advertising same-day retrieval typically return only what's already available electronically, leaving the firm or the client to chase the rest, an experience it says contributes to churn. Codes Health does not market same-day delivery.


Its MIT-educated engineering team keeps building out additional workflows and products, so the platform continues to evolve, improve, and grow more comprehensive as the demands of modern legal practices change. For high-volume customers, it also builds custom integrations with CRM platforms and other medical software, alongside its embedded[Filevine partnership workflow](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/yocierge-vs-chartrequest-vs-codes-health) .


## **Choosing the Right Retrieval Partner for Your Practice**


**Choose ChartRequest when:**


-


Managed retrieval with a dedicated coordinator handling provider follow-up is the core need


-


A 90-day introductory rate suits how you want to trial a vendor


-


Your firm already has chronology and analysis capacity in house or elsewhere


-


Certificates of authenticity and subpoena workflows come up regularly in your cases


-


You want one vendor that also serves the provider side of ROI


**Choose Codes Health when:**


-


You want retrieval and[litigation analysis together](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/best-chartrequest-alternatives) rather than in separate systems


-


Breach-in-care insights and documented future expense extraction matter to your cases


-


Proactive missing record detection before trial is a priority


-


Human verification of AI insights before delivery is a requirement


-


Flat-fee predictability beats a per-request rate that changes after a trial period


-


An embedded Filevine workflow or custom CRM build fits your stack


### **Questions to Ask Any Vendor**


Ask about typical turnaround for complete records rather than just the electronic ones, how the vendor handles providers who don't respond, what the AI does and where it sits in the workflow, how completeness is verified before delivery, what happens to pricing once any promotional period ends, which case management integrations are supported including custom builds, and whether you can talk to references from firms with similar practice areas and caseloads.


## **The Bottom Line**


ChartRequest is a records company that grew up serving healthcare providers and built a legal product on that foundation. The heritage shows in both directions. On the plus side, it means real ROI infrastructure: encryption, double QA verification, redaction, certificates of authenticity, and a team that knows how provider record departments actually operate. On the other, legal is one audience among several, and the published product stops at delivering verified records.


CaseBinder does what it says. A dedicated coordinator chases providers, the team verifies the production against your request, and records land in your dashboard in roughly 14 days by the company's own data. If your firm has the analysis side covered, that may be exactly the scope you want.


If it doesn't, records arriving is only the halfway point. Someone still has to build the chronology, spot the care gaps, and find the expenses that support your damages number.[Codes Health does both](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) , folding that work into the same flat fee as retrieval, with humans checking the AI before anything reaches your case file. Send one active file through and compare what comes back.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What is CaseBinder and how does it differ from ChartRequest's other products?**


CaseBinder is ChartRequest's retrieval product for law firms, offered in Self-Service and Full-Service configurations. ChartRequestPro and ChartRequestComplete are aimed at healthcare organizations managing their own release of information, either in house or fully outsourced. CaseBinder is the one built around requestor-side retrieval for legal teams.


### **How long does ChartRequest take to retrieve medical records?**


ChartRequest reports internal data showing an average of 14 days for CaseBinder retrieval, noting that actual times vary by request and provider. The company also points out that under HIPAA, providers generally have up to 30 days to respond with one possible extension. Codes Health works toward[a complete record set](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) in a couple of weeks, with AI analysis and human verification included in the same workflow.


### **What does CaseBinder cost?**


There's no monthly partnership subscription fee. ChartRequest advertises a 90-day introductory rate of $35 per request with no upfront cost, then moves to custom pricing. Retrieval fees scale with volume, and provider copying fees are separate and vary by jurisdiction. Codes Health uses[flat-fee pricing instead](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/tavrn-vs-chartrequest-vs-codes-health) , combining retrieval with AI review and human-verified insights.


### **Does ChartRequest analyze medical records for litigation?**


ChartRequest retrieves, verifies, redacts, and delivers records. Its public CaseBinder materials do not advertise AI-powered medical chronologies, breach-in-care identification, or future expense extraction. Firms handling[medical malpractice cases](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/llamalab-vs-chartrequest-vs-codes-health) through ChartRequest generally handle that analysis internally or through a separate vendor.


### **What happens when a provider sends incomplete records?**


ChartRequest says its retrieval experts verify that the production matches the request, including patient, date ranges, and record types, and follow up with the provider when records come back incomplete. Codes Health adds proactive AI missing record detection that cross-references patient history to identify gaps before delivery, then works with providers to close them.


### **Is ChartRequest secure and HIPAA compliant?**


ChartRequest advertises 256-bit SSL, 2048-bit private keys, multi-layered AES encryption, role-based access control, and double quality assurance verification on every request, along with SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001-aligned security. Confirm business associate agreement terms and data retention policies directly during evaluation.
